introduction_markdown:
**Time allowed: three hours.** This paper contains six questions arranged in three sections: Section A - Physical and General Chemistry (questions 1 and 2); Section B - Inorganic Chemistry (questions 3 and 4); Section C - Organic Chemistry (questions 5 and 6).

Answer ALL the SIX questions in this booklet. The mark allocation is indicated for each question. Each question carries 20 marks. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Calculators may be used.

**Useful data:** one atmosphere (1 atm) = 1 Pa = $1.01\times10^{5}$ N m$^{-2}$ (as printed); relative atomic masses (RAM): C = 12.0, S = 32.0, O = 16.0, H = 1.0; molar gas volume at stp = 22400 cm$^3$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The halogens are the elements of Group VII (Group 17) of the periodic table (F, Cl, Br, I, At)

(i) Write the outer general electronic configuration of halogens.

(ii) Complete the table below by giving the physical state and colour of the elements.

| | Fluorine | Chlorine | Bromine | Iodine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Physical state | | | | |
| Colour | | | | |

*[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** $ns^2\,np^5$ (seven electrons in the outer shell; e.g. chlorine $[\mathrm{Ne}]\,3s^2\,3p^5$).

**(ii)**

| | Fluorine | Chlorine | Bromine | Iodine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Physical state | gas | gas | liquid | solid |
| Colour | pale yellow | pale green (greenish-yellow) | red-brown | grey-black (violet vapour on warming) |

(at room temperature; the volatility falls and the colour deepens down the group as the van der Waals forces between the $\mathrm{X_2}$ molecules increase).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Chlorine undergoes a disproportionation reaction when reacted with hot concentrated potassium hydroxide.

(i) What is a disproportionation reaction?

(ii) Write down and equation for the disproportionation of chlorine in hot concentrated potassium hydroxide. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A disproportionation reaction is a redox reaction in which **the same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced** (its oxidation state both increases and decreases).

**(ii)** $3\mathrm{Cl_2} + 6\mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow 5\mathrm{KCl} + \mathrm{KClO_3} + 3\mathrm{H_2O}$

Chlorine goes from 0 to $-1$ in KCl (reduced) and from 0 to $+5$ in $\mathrm{KClO_3}$ (oxidised). Check: K 6 = 6, Cl 6 = 6, O 6 = 6, H 6 = 6.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Consider the following hydrogen halides: HF, HCl, HBr, and HI.

(i) Sketch a graph of boiling point for the hydrogen halides

Explain the shape of the graph *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Sketch** (boiling point on the vertical axis, the halides in the order HF, HCl, HBr, HI on the horizontal axis). Approximate values to plot:

| Hydrogen halide | HF | HCl | HBr | HI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boiling point / $^\circ$C | +19.5 | -85 | -67 | -35 |
| Boiling point / K | 293 | 188 | 206 | 238 |

The curve starts **high at HF**, **drops sharply to a minimum at HCl**, then **rises steadily** through HBr to HI.

**Explanation:**

- From HCl to HI the boiling point rises because the molecules have more electrons and are larger, so the instantaneous dipole-induced dipole (van der Waals / London dispersion) forces between molecules are stronger; more energy is needed to separate them.
- HF is anomalously high because fluorine is very small and very electronegative: the H-F bond is strongly polar and molecules are linked by **hydrogen bonds** (F-H...F), which are much stronger than the van der Waals forces in the other halides.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The elements across period 3 of the Periodic Table are Na to Ar.

(i) Complete the table below by giving the formulae of the chlorides formed by the elements.

| Element | Na | Mg | Al | Si | P | S | Cl | Ar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chloride | | | | | | | | |

(ii) Which of the chlorides in d(i) is

A: a solid ionic chloride.

B: a solid covalent chloride

C: a liquid chloride.

(iii) Give the formula of one oxide of the elements which is

A: Giant ionic.

B: Giant molecular.

C: simple molecular *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)**

| Element | Na | Mg | Al | Si | P | S | Cl | Ar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chloride | $\mathrm{NaCl}$ | $\mathrm{MgCl_2}$ | $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ (dimer $\mathrm{Al_2Cl_6}$ in vapour) | $\mathrm{SiCl_4}$ | $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ | $\mathrm{S_2Cl_2}$ (also $\mathrm{SCl_2}$) | none ($\mathrm{Cl_2}$ is the element itself) | none (no compound) |

**(ii)**

- A: solid ionic chloride: **$\mathrm{NaCl}$** (or $\mathrm{MgCl_2}$).
- B: solid covalent chloride: **$\mathrm{AlCl_3}$** (anhydrous, sublimes on heating; $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ is also a solid).
- C: liquid chloride: **$\mathrm{SiCl_4}$** (also $\mathrm{PCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{S_2Cl_2}$ are liquids at room temperature).

**(iii)**

- A: giant ionic oxide: **$\mathrm{Na_2O}$** (or $\mathrm{MgO}$).
- B: giant molecular (giant covalent) oxide: **$\mathrm{SiO_2}$**.
- C: simple molecular oxide: **$\mathrm{SO_2}$** (also $\mathrm{SO_3}$, $\mathrm{P_4O_{10}}$, $\mathrm{P_4O_6}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Sulphur and its compounds are used in the industry and in agriculture.

Give one use of Sulphur and its compounds in the industry and in agriculture

(i) Industry.

(ii) Agriculture. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Industry:** manufacture of **sulphuric acid** by the Contact process (sulphur is burnt to $\mathrm{SO_2}$, which is oxidised to $\mathrm{SO_3}$). Other uses: vulcanisation of rubber, bleaching with sulphur dioxide, matches and gunpowder.

**(ii) Agriculture:** **fungicide** (sulphur powder or copper(II) sulphate in Bordeaux mixture against mildew) and **fertilisers** such as ammonium sulphate, $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}$, and superphosphate (made with sulphuric acid).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give an example of a compound of nitrogen in the -3 and +5 oxidation states

(i) -3.

(ii) +5. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) -3:** ammonia, **$\mathrm{NH_3}$** (N is $-3$ with H = +1); also ammonium chloride $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ or magnesium nitride $\mathrm{Mg_3N_2}$.

**(ii) +5:** nitric acid, **$\mathrm{HNO_3}$** (N: $+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0$, so $x = +5$); also dinitrogen pentoxide $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ or the nitrates such as $\mathrm{KNO_3}$.
